canonicalFacts.claim: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide with an estimated global prevalence of 3.5% in people aged 40-80 years.
High intraocular pressure is a common risk factor for glaucoma, and current standard therapy involves lowering IOP through medical, laser, and/or surgical approaches.
Currently available treatments cannot reverse glaucomatous damage to the visual system, but early diagnosis and treatment can prevent disease progression.
Trabeculectomy is the procedure of choice for surgical control of glaucoma and is often augmented by intraoperative antimetabolite application to reduce scarring.

redFlags: Glaucoma causes irreversible vision loss and requires lifelong management
Early diagnosis is critical as damage cannot be reversed once it occurs
